correctness.rationale: Reconstructed from original RESULT.md Git blob 2231ded6...: writing n=p^a q^b, p<q, rad(n)^2|sigma(n) is exactly p^2|sigma(q^b) and q^2|sigma(p^a). Since sigma(p)=p+1<q^2 and sigma(p^2)=p^2+p+1<q^2, a>=3. For a+b<=5 the complete possible exponent pairs are (3,1),(3,2),(4,1). For (3,2), q cannot divide p+1; then q^2 divides p^2+1<q^2 for odd p, impossible; p=2 gives sigma(8)=15, without odd prime-square divisors. For (3,1), p^2|q+1 implies q>=p^2-1; for p>=3, (p^2-1)^2-sigma(p^3)=p(p^3-p^2-3p-1)>0, checked as positive-coefficient polynomial after p=t+3. p=2 cannot give q^2|15. For (4,1), q+1=kp^2. If k>=2, q^2>=(2p^2-1)^2>sigma(p^4), with the last difference 3p^4-p^3-5p^2-p positive after p=t+2. Thus k=1 and q=p^2-1, composite for odd p; p=2 gives q=3 and 9∤31. Finally sigma(96)=252, rad(96)^2=36, 252/36=7, Omega=6. No other exponent case is omitted.
residual_risks: Finite verifier covers only p<q<=5000; the universal theorem is derived from the symbolic case split, not enumeration.
No uniqueness at Omega=6, or solution classification beyond the minimum, is claimed.

originality.rationale: The exact predicate and the witness 96 predate the submission: the 2012 source studies gamma(n)^2|sigma(n) in its final remarks, and OEIS A173615 tabulates the same predicate. The claimed new part is the uniform unbounded exclusion of all p^a q^b, p<q, with a+b<=5, not the predicate, the example 96, or the fixed {2,3} characterization. The two accessible relevant primary texts and OEIS entry were compared at the level of hypotheses and implications; none of the inspected statements establishes the all-prime-pair exponent cutoff. This is a best-of-knowledge assessment, not certification of priority.
residual_risks: A173615 established the exact predicate and witness 96 before the finding; the only candidate novelty is the uniform bound for arbitrary two-prime supports.
An equivalent six-factor exclusion might exist in an unindexed elementary note or problem discussion, or follow implicitly from an unexamined stronger paper.
The search of published SCOPE code and Resultary is bounded, not a proof of absence.

value.rationale: The precise first Omega layer is a motivated structural invariant of the two-prime-support component of the reverse core-square divisor-sum problem explicitly considered by Broughan et al. and tabulated in OEIS A173615. A magnitude-ordered table showing 96 first cannot preclude arbitrarily large p^a q^b of smaller total exponent. The theorem gives a uniform cross-support obstruction and proves the exact optimal total multiplicity 6. Its contribution is modest and elementary, but supplies a size-independent cutoff a future classification or search over all prime pairs can rely on; it is neither an arbitrary slice nor a known-table recomputation.
residual_risks: The elementary character of the cutoff limits its breadth; it does not classify all Omega=6 or arbitrary prime-support solutions.
The witness 96 and the identical sequence predicate were already known, and alone contribute no new value.
